reasons: No pass or fail checks; it prints numbers for a person to judge.
The project ID and name are hardcoded.
The pre-fix queries are a hand copy of old behavior, not the original code.
Writes to the database when RUN_JOB is set to 1.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and fixed project settings
sections.what: Loads the database, storage, search router and query builder, and fixes the project ID, name and country used in the test.
sections.why: Keeps the measurement pointed at one real project so runs can be compared.
sections.watch_out: The project ID is hardcoded, so the script only works for that project in that database.

sections.name: evidenceCount
sections.title: Counting evidence rows
sections.what: Counts how many evidence rows the Jeddah project currently has.
sections.why: Gives a before number and an after number to show whether a research run added evidence.
sections.watch_out: The count covers all evidence rows for the project, not only rows added by this run.

sections.name: oldTierDomains
sections.title: Trusted domains before the fix
sections.what: Lists up to ten trusted website domains from the sources table, with no industry filter.
sections.why: Recreates what the old code would have loaded, so the before run is realistic.
sections.watch_out: If the database query changes, the before numbers no longer reflect the old behavior.

sections.name: newTierDomains
sections.title: Trusted domains after the fix
sections.what: Lists up to ten trusted domains that match this project's industry.
sections.why: Matches the fixed behavior, where the industry limits which sources are used.
sections.watch_out: Returns an empty list if the project has no industry set.

sections.name: preFixQueries
sections.title: Rebuilding the old query list
sections.what: Builds the old set of queries: a general news query, a construction query with the country, and up to three site-restricted queries, capped at eight.
sections.why: Likely reason: the comments say nuclear terms were not added for this project, so the old list had no industry-specific terms. Otherwise not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: This is a hand copy of the old logic, so it can drift from what the app really used.

sections.name: measure
sections.title: Running and measuring a query set
sections.what: Runs each query through the router and counts raw results, unique URLs and unique domains. Prints each query's result count and any errors.
sections.why: Passes the industry value that each code path really uses, so the comparison is fair.
sections.watch_out: Errors are caught and printed as a zero-result line, so a failing query can look like a quiet one.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Running the full measurement
sections.what: Counts evidence, builds both query sets, measures both, prints a summary, and optionally runs a real research job and reports the change in evidence rows.
sections.why: Puts the steps in the order a reader needs to judge the fix.
sections.watch_out: Setting RUN_JOB to 1 is the only step that writes to the database, because it starts a real research job.

summary: A manual measurement script that compares search results for one real project before and after a retrieval fix, and can optionally run a real research job to count new evidence rows.
purpose: Gives evidence that the query-building fix changed the search results for the Jeddah Central Arena project.
why: Likely reason: the fix was made to query building for non-nuclear projects, so this run checks the fix against the live search router. Reason for the RUN_JOB option not stated in the code.
how: Counts evidence rows, loads the project, rebuilds the old query set and builds the new one, runs both through the live search router, and prints totals. If RUN_JOB is set to 1, it runs a real research job and counts evidence rows again.
inputs: The hardcoded project ID and name, the sources table, the project record, the live search router, and the RUN_JOB environment variable.
outputs: Console output only: result counts per query, unique URLs and domains, a summary, and optionally the change in evidence rows. No files are written.
risks: With RUN_JOB set to 1, the script creates and runs a real research job, which writes evidence rows to the database. The pre-fix query set is rebuilt by hand, so the before numbers are an approximation of the old code.
debug: If counts are zero, check the sources table for enabled tier 1 or tier 2 rows and check the search router settings. If the script fails at startup, check the database connection. Compare the printed query lists with the expected project name.
